newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin says October budget update likely.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin says October budget update likely.

text.p: Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Monday he would probably present his autumn budget update in October.

Markets will be watching that for a final word on the performance in the 1996-97 fiscal year and for signs of how quickly Canada will balance its budget. He said the next budget should be unveiled toward the end of February.
He made the remarks to the Canadian Broadcasting Corp.
Asked if possible rising interest rates might not throw off Ottawa's deficit targets, he said: "Interest rates going up do affect the deficit."

But he added: "The only way that you're going to have a rise in interest rates is if in fact the fundamentals require it -- if your growth is really very, very strong or if there are inflationary pressures."
He did not mention the possibility of the Bank of Canada raising rates in reaction to U.S. hikes, but said it was encouraging that there was growth without inflation.

"One of the things that we have seen in the United States is that in fact you can have strong growth and very, very few inflationary pressures. That really is what's happening there, and that's why all of us are very optimistic that we're in for a very long period of sustained growth."
